title: Advanced Analysis for Modern Heavy Music
description: Non-functional harmony, unusual meter, riff-as-harmony, and an analysis method that does not force a chorale onto a blast-beat song.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 21M.350 Musical Analysis
sourceReferences.notes: Form and analysis as a method. We reuse the method on riff-based music rather than copying the repertoire.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 21M.302
sourceReferences.notes: Chromatic craft is the last common-practice tool this course still needs.

modules.title: Beyond function
modules.blurb: Planing, mediants, modes that refuse a dominant.
learningObjectives: Write harmony that does not report to a dominant
Name planing, tritone, and modal tonic as alternatives to V–I

modules.title: Meter that lies
learningObjectives: Group an odd bar, a hemiola, or two meters that meet later
Displace a cell without rewriting its pitches

modules.title: Riff as harmony
learningObjectives: Treat the riff as the progression and the form
Analyze by cell and contrast, not by inventing a chorale

concepts.name: Non-functional harmony
concepts.summary: Progression that does not report to a dominant.
objectives: Write a progression that does not report to a dominant
Analyze it without inventing a V–I that is not there

concepts.name: Planing
concepts.summary: A shape that slides, keeping its intervals.
objectives: Slide a shape so the intervals stay and the function does not
Write a parallel move that is the harmony, not a voice-leading error

concepts.name: Chromatic mediants
concepts.summary: Roots a third apart, few common tones, a lot of color.
objectives: Connect roots a third apart with few common tones
Hear the color of that jump without forcing a pivot

concepts.name: Tritone relationships
concepts.summary: The interval that bisects the octave.
objectives: Use the interval that bisects the octave as a relation, not an accident
Write a tritone substitution or a tritone riff cell on purpose

concepts.name: Locrian and the diminished tonic
concepts.summary: A mode whose tonic triad is already unstable.
objectives: Sit on a tonic whose triad is already diminished
Predict why Locrian is unstable as a home and useful as a color

concepts.name: Phrygian and the flat second
concepts.summary: The half-step above the tonic as a signature.
objectives: Use the flat second against the tonic as a signature
Write a Phrygian cell that does not secretly cadence in the relative major

concepts.name: Harmonic minor as a metal default
concepts.summary: The raised seventh without the rest of the classical contract.
objectives: Raise the seventh in minor without taking on the rest of the classical contract
Write a metal default that wants the leading tone and the minor third

concepts.name: Octatonic collections
concepts.summary: Alternating tones and semitones, two flavors.
objectives: Build an octatonic collection from alternating tones and semitones
Predict the two flavors and a diminished cell that lives inside them

concepts.name: Odd meter
concepts.summary: Bars that are not 2 or 4 on the surface.
objectives: Group a bar that is not 2 or 4 on the surface
Feel 7 as 3+2+2 or 2+2+3 rather than as 'hard 4'

concepts.name: Polymeter
concepts.summary: Two meters at once, coinciding later.
objectives: Run two meters at once and mark where they coincide
Write guitar in 3 against a kit in 4 that meets after a known span

concepts.name: Metric ambiguity
concepts.summary: A pulse you cannot yet group.
objectives: Write a pulse the ear cannot yet group
Resolve or refuse that ambiguity on purpose

concepts.name: Rhythmic displacement
concepts.summary: The same cell, started on a different beat.
objectives: Start the same cell on a different beat
Predict how the accents flip when the cell moves by one eighth

concepts.name: Hemiola and 3:2
concepts.summary: Three in the time of two, or the reverse.
objectives: Write three in the time of two, or the reverse
Clap a hemiola that is not just a triplet fill

concepts.name: Riff-based harmony
concepts.summary: The riff is the progression.
objectives: Treat the riff as the progression
Analyze a section by the cell, not by a chord chart you invented

concepts.name: Pedal-tone riffs
concepts.summary: An open string that everything else grinds against.
objectives: Grind changing figures against an open string
Write a pedal riff whose clashes release

concepts.name: Chromatic riff cells
concepts.summary: Semitone motion as the material, not the decoration.
objectives: Use semitone motion as the material, not the decoration
Sequence a two-note chromatic cell without turning it into a scale run

concepts.name: Cluster and close dissonance
concepts.summary: Seconds stacked until the chord has no name.
objectives: Stack seconds until the chord has no common-practice name
Decide whether that cluster is the harmony or a passing smear

concepts.name: Form built from riffs
concepts.summary: Contrast and return without a verse-chorus contract.
objectives: Build form from contrast and return of cells, not from verse-chorus
Mark a section change that is only a drum texture and a new cell

concepts.name: What analysis is for
concepts.summary: A method: what repeats, what contrasts, what is the cell.
objectives: Ask what repeats, what contrasts, and what the cell is
Refuse an analysis that invents a chorale the music does not play

concepts.name: Reduction without forcing a chorale
concepts.summary: Strip the surface. Do not invent a I–V that is not there.
objectives: Strip the surface without inventing a I–V that is not there
Leave a reduction that still explains the riff

concepts.name: Distortion as a harmonic fact
concepts.summary: Gain adds partials. A fifth becomes a crowd.
objectives: Treat gain as a harmonic fact that adds partials
Predict why a fifth becomes a crowd under distortion

concepts.name: Drop tunings and string physics
concepts.summary: A lowered sixth string that makes the power chord one finger.
objectives: Lower a string so a power chord is one finger, and write for that physics
Predict what the new open string does to pedals and cells
